Below is a quick‑reference list of the **long weekends** that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a public holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday (or a holiday that, when combined with a weekend, gives you three consecutive days off).  Provincial holidays that create a long weekend are shown under the province(s) where they apply.

| Date | Holiday | Province(s) | Notes |
|------|---------|-------------|-------|
| **Feb 20** | Family Day | Ontario, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island | Monday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Mar 17** | St. Patrick’s Day | Newfoundland & Labrador | Friday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | All provinces | Friday – 3‑day weekend |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | All provinces | Monday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Jun 23** | Manitoba Day | Manitoba | Thursday – *not* a statutory holiday; no long weekend |
| **Jun 24** | St. Jean‑Baptiste Day | Quebec | Thursday – *not* a statutory holiday; no long weekend |
| **Jul 1** | Canada Day | All provinces | Saturday – no long weekend |
| **Aug 7** | BC Day | British Columbia | Monday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Aug 14** | Saskatchewan Day | Saskatchewan | Monday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Aug 21** | Heritage Day | Alberta | Monday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | All provinces | Monday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | All provinces | Monday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Nov 11** | Remembrance Day | All provinces | Saturday – no long weekend |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas Day | All provinces | Monday – 3‑day weekend |
| **Dec 26** | Boxing Day | All provinces | Tuesday – no long weekend |

### Quick Summary

| Province | Long Weekend Holidays (2023) |
|----------|------------------------------|
| **Alberta** | Family Day (Feb 20), Heritage Day (Aug 21), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **British Columbia** | Family Day (Feb 20), BC Day (Aug 7), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **Manitoba** | Family Day (Feb 20), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **New Brunswick** | Family Day (Feb 20), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **Newfoundland & Labrador** | St. Patrick’s Day (Mar 17), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **Nova Scotia** | Family Day (Feb 20), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **Ontario** | Family Day (Feb 20), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **Prince Edward Island** | Family Day (Feb 20), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **Quebec** | Family Day (Feb 20), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |
| **Saskatchewan** | Family Day (Feb 20), Saskatchewan Day (Aug 14), Labour Day (Sep 4), Thanksgiving (Oct 9), Christmas (Dec 25) |

> **Tip for your app:**  
> - If you want to highlight *all* long weekends regardless of province, you can simply list the dates above.  
> - If you want to filter by province, use the province‑specific table.  
> - Remember that some holidays (e.g., St. Jean‑Baptiste Day in Quebec or Manitoba Day) are **not** statutory holidays, so they do not create a long weekend unless you add a personal day off.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the data in a different format (JSON, CSV, etc.) or if you need additional details such as the exact day of the week for each holiday.
